title: Enterprise Onboarding, Support Process, Health Checks & QBR Playbook
author: Priya Natarajan
body:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's enterprise onboarding checklist, integration guidance, escalation procedures, known issues and workarounds, and the cadence and content for health checks and Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs). It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers, Support Engineers, and SRE partners responsible for onboarding and operating enterprise customers.

Goals:
- Shorten time-to-value for new enterprise customers
- Standardize escalation and support handoffs to meet SLA commitments
- Provide a repeatable health-check and QBR cadence that surfaces regressions and optimization opportunities

Scope:
- Applies to all Dedicated and Private deployment onboarding flows and high-touch Hosted enterprise accounts
- Integrations with customer systems (webhooks, VPC peering, KMS), model rollouts, and runtime configuration are covered
- Excludes low-touch free-tier signups and community trial accounts

Audience:
- Customer Success (owner)
- Solutions Engineering (integration lead)
- Support & SRE (operational support and escalation)
- Product/Platform (for roadmap inputs surfaced in QBR)

Roles & Ownership:

| Role | Primary responsibilities | Escalation contact | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| CSM | Customer relationship, QBR facilitation, adoption tracking | N/A | N/A |
| Solutions Engineer | Integration runbook, onboarding workshop, data mapping | se-oncall@redwood.ai | 8 business hours |
| Support Engineer | Tier 1/2 triage, incident intake, workarounds | support@redwood.ai | 1 hour (P1), 4 hours (P2) |
| SRE / Infra | Capacity, network, private deployment orchestration | sre-oncall@redwood.ai | 30 minutes (P1) |
| Product Manager | Feature/bug prioritization post-QBR | product@redwood.ai | N/A |

Onboarding checklist (high-level):
1. Pre-onboarding (CSM + Sales)
   - Confirm contract terms, deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), and data residency requirements
   - Collect technical contacts, network contacts, and security team details
   - Share onboarding schedule and pre-reqs doc (link to integration checklist)

2. Day 0 — Environment & Access
   - Provision account and invite primary contacts to Console
   - For Dedicated/Private: validate VPC peering, firewall rules (egress to 13.35.0.0/16), and KMS connectivity
   - Issue API keys and verify basic generate/embeddings calls against a small test prompt set

3. Day 1 — Integration Workshop
   - Run integration workshop with Solutions Engineer: routes, auth, request patterns, batching needs, and expected traffic profile
   - Confirm model selection and quantization profile plan (link to quantization-profiles)
   - Establish observability hooks (trace IDs, request tagging, logging endpoints)

4. Week 1 — Validation & Load Tests
   - Execute smoke tests and a staged load test (target 1-2x expected peak)
   - Validate latency and throughput against contractual SLOs (see SLO table)
   - Create an eval/prompt-set to baseline quality metrics for later QBR comparisons

5. Week 2-4 — Optimization & Handover
   - Implement batching, prefix caching config, and autoscaling policies recommended by Redwood Optimize
   - Document runbook for common operational events and escalation points
   - Handover to Support for ongoing operations and schedule first monthly health check

Onboarding workshop agenda (suggested):
- 00:00-00:15: Introductions, objectives, success metrics
- 00:15-00:45: Architecture review & network requirements
- 00:45-01:30: Integration walkthrough (API, auth, telemetry)
- 01:30-02:00: Model/quality discussion and evaluation plan
- 02:00-02:15: Rollout plan and next steps

SLOs & Thresholds (production targets):

| Metric | Target | Measurement | Escalation threshold |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| 99th percentile latency (text-gen, 0-512 tokens) | <= 250 ms | per-route latency dashboard | > 400 ms sustained 15m |
| p50 latency | <= 75 ms | per-route latency dashboard | > 150 ms |
| Request success rate | >= 99.9% | error-rate alert (5m window) | < 99.0% |
| Token-level cost variance vs baseline | <= 20% | cost-per-token analytics | > 35% |

Escalation playbook (TL;DR):
- Severity definitions: P1 (service-impacting: outage or major degradation), P2 (partial degradation impacting important customers), P3 (minor impact), P4 (cosmetic/ops request)
- Contact matrix: support@redwood.ai -> Support triage -> SRE/Infra or SE oncall as required -> CSM for customer comms

Step-by-step escalation procedure:
1. Triage (Support): Confirm scope, affected customers, and whether Dedicated/Private or Hosted. Gather request-id, example payloads, and recent trace-ids.
2. Classification: Map to severity and tag the ticket with severity label and product area (runtime, routing, auth, model-quality).
3. Immediate mitigations (examples):
   - For latency regressions: switch traffic to a lower-latency model variant or enable aggressive batching fallback (SE/SRE action)
   - For auth/network failures: confirm VPC routes, DNS resolution, and KMS availability; provide temporary API key if required
   - For model-quality regressions: revert to pinned model version and open model-quality incident with Applied ML team
4. Escalate: If unresolved past the escalation threshold (see SLA table), page the oncall SRE and SE teams.
5. Communication: CSM to send initial incident update within 30 minutes for P1, hourly thereafter until resolved.
6. Post-incident: Owner creates a postmortem within 3 business days; PM and Product/Research invited for RCA and remediation planning.

Example escalation SMS/email templates (Support -> SRE oncall):
- Subject: [REDWOOD P1] {customer-name} - API outage - {region}
- Body: Severity: P1
  Affected customer: {customer-name}
  Summary: {one-line summary}
  Key traces: {trace-ids}
  Repro: {steps}
  Attachments: logs, error-rate graph URL

Known issues & workarounds (selected):

| ID | Symptom | Root cause (short) | Workaround / Mitigation | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| KI-2026-01 | Intermittent 502s for streaming responses | HTTP keepalive exhaustion in older gateway image | Restart gateway pod; upgrade to gateway v2.1.3; enable per-connection backpressure | Eng Platform |
| KI-2026-07 | Embedding drift after model swap | Missing normalization pre-processing in customer pipeline | Apply our normalization snippet: text.lower().strip() + unicode_normalize; roll back model if severe | Applied ML |
| KI-2026-12 | High per-token cost for long context windows | Customers sending full document on every request instead of using prefix caching | Configure prefix caching and delta updates; recommend using embedding-store for large archives | Solutions Eng |

Support process & ticket lifecycle:
- Intake: All enterprise tickets route to Zendesk queue "Enterprise Support" with tags: customer_id, deployment_mode, severity
- Triage SLA: 1 hour for P1/P2, 4 hours for P3, 2 business days for P4
- Ownership: Support owns ticket until mitigation is applied; for platform-side issues, SRE takes operational ownership with Support as communications lead
- Escalation thresholds: If ticket is not mitigated within the SLA window, support engineer must notify CSM and page SRE oncall

Diagnostic checklist (triage common items):
- Confirm customer account and route the request to correct region/cluster
- Run: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health and save response
- Check per-route latency and error graphs in Console (last 30 minutes)
- For Dedicated/Private: verify VPC peering BGP status and KMS key availability
- Check recent deploys (last 24 hours) and model rollouts

Health check & QBR cadence:
- Weekly health check (CSM + Support): 30-minute sync covering high-severity items, usage trends, and cost anomalies. Attendees: CSM, SE, Support lead, Customer PO.
- Monthly operational review: 60-minute meeting focused on adoption metrics, error trends, and capacity planning. Provide action items and owners.
- Quarterly Business Review (QBR):
  - Pre-QBR deliverables (2 weeks prior): latest adoption dashboard, model quality evals, cost breakdown, open issues and remediation plan
  - QBR attendees: Customer executive sponsor, CSM, Solutions Eng, Product PM, Applied ML lead, SRE representative
  - QBR agenda:
    1) Business outcomes & success metrics update
    2) Usage trends & cost summary (tokens per user, model cost)
    3) Quality & regressions (prompt-set evals vs baseline)
    4) Roadmap and feature asks
    5) Action items and prioritization

QBR metrics (suggested):
- Adoption: MAU using Redwood features, API calls per user, successful session rate
- Performance: p50/p95/p99 latency by route, error rate trend
- Quality: prompt-set pass rate, hallucination incidents per 10k requests
- Cost: cost per 1k tokens, percent savings from batching/caching

Example queries & dashboard widgets (high-level):
- Total API calls (30d), broken down by route and model variant
- 99th percentile latency heatmap (by hour) for last 30 days
- Top 10 customers by token usage and trendline
- Model quality eval: pass/fail counts for canonical prompt set

Operational runbooks & artifacts to deliver during onboarding:
- Integration runbook (API keys, example calls, SDK snippets)
- Network & security checklist for Dedicated/Private
- Baseline evaluation prompt-set and automated eval harness (link to eval-harness)
- Incident response playbook (this document is the canonical source)

Appendix: Useful commands & examples
- Health check: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health | jq '.'
- Example generation call (curl):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"model":"redwood-1-small", "input":"Hello world", "max_tokens":64}'

- Example logging filter (Console): trace_id:"{trace-id}" AND route:"/v1/generate" AND level:ERROR

Document maintenance:
- Owner: Customer Success (Priya Natarajan)
- Review cadence: Quarterly (align with QBR schedule). Update after major infra changes (e.g., gateway upgrade, new model runtime) or post-incident learning that affects onboarding or escalation steps.
